predecessors.note: The Lintun page: 'established as part of Youzhou by Han dynasty' in 108 BCE (the Four Commanderies page has 107 BCE). The east coast was Ye land; the page names no state.

land.text: Lintun, whose 'border is almost the same as the current Gangwon Province' (Lintun page), main office Dongyi prefecture (Gangneung)

successors.note: Nine of fifteen prefectures were abolished in 82 BCE (Lintun page); the Dongye dossier (jk-02-a, Eastern Ye page) has the Ye independent from 82 BCE.

land.text: the prefectures that stayed after 82 BCE (new Dongyi at Wonsan, Buer at Anbyon)

successors.note: 'In 82 BCE Lintun was merged into Xuantu' (Four Commanderies page, Bowman); the Lintun page's own text has seven prefectures including Fuzu incorporated into Lelang, and Bowman has parts of old Lintun merged into Lelang about 75 BCE.

capitals.name: Dongyi prefecture (Gangneung)
capitals.note: 'Dongyi prefecture (Gangneung City, Gangwon) was the main office.'

capitals.name: New Dongyi prefecture (Wonsan)
capitals.note: After incorporation the main office is given as new Dongyi at Wonsan (and, in the same table, Buer at Anbyon); the page does not reconcile the two.

correction.text: Lintun, whose 'border is almost the same as the current Gangwon Province' (Lintun page), main office Dongyi prefecture (Gangneung)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). The page's boundary is 'almost the same as the current Gangwon Province' and it names Huali prefecture in Kumya County, South Hamgyong, and prefectures at Gangneung, Sokcho, Anbyon, Wonsan, Munchon and Goseong; nine more are 'somewhere in present-day Gangwon Province'. It also reports a revisionist placement in the southern Liaodong peninsula, unrecognized in US, Chinese and Japanese academia. No area on the page; no comparison possible. Cliopatria's Dongye row (-91..) draws the same coast as Ye land.

region.text: Lintun, whose 'border is almost the same as the current Gangwon Province' (Lintun page), main office Dongyi prefecture (Gangneung)

ledger.note: 108 BCE: the Han found Lintun on the east coast. 'In BCE 108, Lintun Commandery was established as part of Youzhou by Han dynasty.' The Four Commanderies page has 107 BCE for Lintun and Zhenfan. The extent is the page's 'almost the same as the current Gangwon Province'.

region.text: Lintun, whose 'border is almost the same as the current Gangwon Province' (Lintun page), main office Dongyi prefecture (Gangneung)

ledger.note: 82 BCE: most of Lintun is abandoned. 'In 82 BCE, 9 prefectures out of 15 had been abolished' and 'At this point, Lintun Commandery was disappeared from history.' The Ye taking the land is the dongye dossier's reading of the Eastern Ye page ('Become independent in 82 BC'); the Lintun page does not mention the Ye.

region.text: the prefectures that stayed after 82 BCE (new Dongyi at Wonsan, Buer at Anbyon)

ledger.note: 82 BCE: the rest of Lintun is merged into Xuantu. Four Commanderies page: 'In 82 BCE, Lintun was absorbed into Xuantu' and 'Lintun was transferred to Lelang in 75 BCE'; the Lintun page's own text: '7 prefectures including Fuzu/Bujo (夫租) prefecture were incorporated to Lelang Commandery'. The two accounts are not reconciled; the Four Commanderies chain is followed.

region.text: Lintun, whose 'border is almost the same as the current Gangwon Province' (Lintun page), main office Dongyi prefecture (Gangneung)

ledger.note: 82 BCE: Lintun ends. Seven of its fifteen prefectures survive in Xuantu and Lelang; the east coast returns to the Ye.

wars.name: Han conquest of Wiman Joseon
wars.outcome: The Han destroy Wiman Chosŏn in 108 BCE and set up Lelang, Lintun and Zhenfan (Four Commanderies page).
wars.note: Lintun was set up from the Ye coast, which the Wiman state held on the Eastern Ye page's account (not opened here).

certainty.note: The page gives a modern province and a list of prefectures, no boundary.

sources.title: Lintun Commandery
sources.note: Founding 108 BCE, Gangwon extent, prefectures, 82 BCE abolition; Bowman on the merger with Xuantu.

sources.title: Four Commanderies of Han
sources.note: 107 BCE-82 BCE; absorbed into Xuantu in 82; transferred to Lelang in 75.

notes: Colony dossier of 26 years; no Cliopatria row. Cliopatria's Han Dynasty (-91..) shape contains the coast; its Dongye row starts -91, nine years before the dongye dossier (jk-02-a) starts the Ye at -82, so the Ye are drawn inside Lintun for -91..-83. The dongye dossier's -82 found event names han-dynasty as counterpart; this dossier names dongye as the counterpart of the loss. The Lintun page and the Four Commanderies page differ on the start (108 against 107 BCE) and on where the remnant went (Lelang against Xuantu). Gangneung and Wonsan are gazetteer places; 'Kangwŏn-do' is the North Korean province.
